query_meta.method: GraphQL target.associatedDiseases(size=2000); filtered to liver/steatosis disease terms; datatypeScores inspected for genetic_association vs literature
query_meta.interpretation_note: For a disease row, datatypeScores lists ONLY datatypes with non-zero evidence. The ABSENCE of a 'genetic_association' key for a steatosis term means Open Targets holds NO human genetic evidence linking that gene to that term.

key_finding: For all three hepatic fatty-acid-uptake proteins, Open Targets v4 associations to MASLD/steatosis terms are driven ENTIRELY by the 'literature' (text-mining) datatype. No 'genetic_association' datatype score is present for non-alcoholic fatty liver, MASH, steatosis, or fatty liver disease for SLC27A5, SLC27A2, or CD36. CD36's higher overall score reflects greater literature prominence, not human genetic support.

slc27a5_liver_disease_footprint_top_over.disease: neonatal intrahepatic cholestasis due to citrin deficiency (MONDO_0011601)

slc27a5_footprint_note: FATP5's strongest human liver-disease associations are CHOLESTATIC / bile-acid phenotypes, consistent with its bile-acid-CoA ligase (BACS) moonlighting function, not with a steatosis-uptake role. This is a pleiotropy/confound signal relevant to interpreting FATP5 knockout steatosis phenotypes.

genetic_association_scores_observed.note: No genetic_association score to any specific MASLD/steatosis/MASH term for any of the three genes.
